newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down on year-end US dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down on year-end US dlr demand.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly lower against its American counterpart on Friday on exporters' year-end demand for U.S. dollars, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at T$27.505, off a low of T$27.515, against Thursday's T$27.503 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$316 million.

Dealers noted some speculative activity trying to push the Taiwan dollar lower after late morning news that foreign orders for Taiwan goods in November had fallen 4.16 percent to US$10.027 billion compared to November 1995.
"Poor export performance tends to give pressure on the Taiwan dollar to fall due to a possible lessening of U.S. dollar supply," said one dealer.
"However, exporters, who have kept a lot of U.S. dollar stocks due to recent sluggish trade, actively entered to sell U.S. dollars when the Taiwan dollar fell below T$27.51."
The exporters' move largely offset the local dollar's depreciation, he added.
For Saturday, a stable T$27.495-27.515 range was seen.
